content.text:
Let me analyze this ticket.

Employee: Jennifer Miller (E017)
Request: write access to Source Code

Notes:
- Notes 1-5 say she's a full-time Analyst, maximum for full-time employees is write (admin only if role owns the system; Analyst doesn't own Source Code, Engineer role does). So write is allowed.
- Note 6 from Security DB says she's a contractor with basic security training. Contractors: read, or write if advanced security training. Never admin. Basic training means max is read. So requested write exceeds maximum, grant read.

There's a conflict: 5 notes say full-time, 1 note (Security) says contractor. The security note says "Security DB records Jennifer Miller (E017) as a contractor with basic security training." Hmm.

Which is more reliable? The team memory has conflicting facts. As the Approver, I need to make a decision. Security DB typically has the most authoritative employment classification? Actually, HR is typically authoritative for employment type. But here we have conflict.

Let me think. Most notes (HR, IT, Finance, Compliance, Facilities) say full-time. Security says contractor. The facilities and compliance notes rely on HR/IT notes. The IT database confirms Analyst full-time per HR note. Finance confirms role Analyst; HR/IT confirm full-time.

Security DB is the only one saying contractor. Could be an error, or could be the accurate one. The security note mentions "Security DB records Jennifer Miller (E017) as a contractor with basic security training."

Hmm, how to resolve? Typically, HR is the source of truth for employment status. Multiple independent notes (or at least HR + IT) confirm full-time. Security note contradicts. But maybe the security DB is more current? There's no indication of that.

I think the majority/HR authority suggests full-time, which allows write. The requested level is write, which equals max for full-time. So grant write.

Actually, let's be careful. The policy: full_time employees up to write, admin only if role owns system. Analyst doesn't own Source Code (Engineer owns). So max = write. Requested = write. Grant write.

If contractor with basic training, max = read, so grant read.

The conflict. I'll go with the full-time classification per HR (authoritative for employment type) and the majority of notes. Grant write.

Let me submit write.
